He had to take part in gatherings of prominent citizens, at which campaigners were designated and then distributed among the villages and city wards. The citizens argued loudly. He sat to the side and was silent, as if it had nothing to do with him. This stupid passivity worried him. He opened his mouth to say something, to object, but one of the staff always grabbed him by the hand and told him in a patronizing, fatherly tone, “You just be quiet. Stay on the sidelines.
